captions.headline: The scary stat about ATS rejection is mostly made up. The real story is harder.
captions.subline: Recruiters do not auto-reject. They run out of time. Make your CV the one that earns the minute.
captions.caption_linkedin:
You have probably seen the number. Seventy-five percent of resumes never reach a human. The Applicant Tracking System filters you out before a recruiter ever sees your name.

It turns out the number is mostly invented.

A 2025 study traced the original claim to a 2012 sales pitch from a startup that went out of business in 2013. The same study, surveying 25 US recruiters across more than 10 ATS platforms, found that 92 percent of them do not configure auto-rejection rules based on resume content.

The ATS is not the villain you were told it was. The real story is harder, and it is this: recruiters are looking at hundreds of CVs for one role and they have minutes, not hours. The CV that does not state clearly, in the first six lines, why you are the right fit for this specific role is the CV that gets closed and forgotten.

The fix is the same regardless of which version of the story is true. Tailor the top of your CV to the role. State the job title you are applying for. State one quantified outcome that proves you can do it. Save the rest of your history for paragraph two.

Spark Careers does that tailoring for you, role by role, in five minutes.

captions.headline: Sixty-two percent of hiring managers reject AI resumes that lack personalization.
captions.subline: AI assistance is fine. Generic AI output is not.
captions.caption_facebook:
If you have been using ChatGPT or a generic AI to write your applications, here is data worth knowing.

A 2026 hiring survey found that 62 percent of US hiring managers reject AI-written resumes that lack personalization. Forty-nine percent will auto-dismiss any CV they suspect was generated by AI. Recruiters notice the same five hedge phrases, the same three-paragraph structure, the same generic tone.

This is not an argument against using AI. AI is a real productivity tool for job hunters. It is an argument against shipping AI output without your fingerprints on it.

The pattern that works: use AI to draft the structure and tailor the keywords. Then rewrite every bullet in your own voice. Add the one specific detail only you would know about the role you did.

Spark Careers does the structure and keyword tailoring for you. The personalization is on you. We make the time exist. https://spark.risepointcareers.com/?utm_source=social&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=w25-tue-b2c

captions.headline: Forty-nine percent of hiring managers auto-dismiss resumes that look AI-written.
captions.subline: If your CV sounds like everyone else's, it gets treated like everyone else's.
captions.caption_linkedin:
Forty-nine percent of US hiring managers say they auto-dismiss resumes that read like AI wrote them.

There are patterns recruiters recognize after the third one in a stack. The opening line that calls you a 'results-driven professional.' The bullet that says you 'leveraged cross-functional stakeholders to drive impact.' The summary that lists the same six skills the job description listed, in the same order.

None of that came from you. Hiring managers can tell.

This is the strange new world for job seekers. AI tools are a real productivity gain when used well. They are a real liability when used as a copy-paste shortcut. The difference is whether the final draft sounds like a specific person who did specific things.

A quick test: read the first paragraph of your CV out loud. If you would not say those exact sentences to a friend at dinner, rewrite them.

Spark Careers does the keyword tailoring against each job. The voice on the page is yours.

captions.subline: The team you build this season will outlast the cycle.
captions.caption_linkedin:

The job openings number went up. The competition for the candidates you want went up with it. Every other small business in your category is starting to hire again at the same time you are.

This is the part of the cycle where it is tempting to either rush a hire or freeze entirely. Both are mistakes. The companies that come out of a hot quarter with a team they actually wanted are the ones that kept the process tight even when the temptation was to skip steps.

Four habits that hold up across cycles. Reply on day one. Be honest about what the role actually is. Reference check the person you are about to extend an offer to. Make the decision on the second instinct, not the first.

Nothing about the market changes those four. Spark Careers Enterprise just makes them easier to do consistently when the inbox is full.

captions.headline: Two to three percent of applications become interviews. The right thirty matter more than the wrong three hundred.
captions.subline: Apply with intent. Tailor with care. The math rewards the disciplined.
captions.caption_linkedin:
A ratio worth pinning above your job search desk.

Research on application conversion is consistent across surveys: only two to three percent of applications result in an interview. Ninety-seven to ninety-eight percent never get a recruiter view that lasts longer than five seconds.

The instinct, when those numbers land, is to apply more. Send the same CV to a hundred more roles. Hope volume fixes it.

Volume does not fix it. Tailoring fixes it.

The math on a tailored funnel looks like this. Thirty roles you actually want. Twenty that you can write a real CV for. Five interviews. One or two final rounds. One offer.

The math on a spray-and-pray funnel looks like this. Three hundred roles you do not really want. Six interviews, all for jobs you would not take. Zero offers that pay.

The disciplined path is slower for two weeks and faster from week three. Keep going.

Free. https://spark.risepointcareers.com/?utm_source=social&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=w25-thu-b2c
